requirement: Connect dispatch planning and execution through the public dispatch entry.
finding: src/dispatch/index.mjs re-exports eleven dispatch modules but never re-exports src/dispatch/executor.mjs or src/dispatch/runtime.mjs, so the execution operations added for this issue (executeAuthorizedPlan, executeDryRun, emitPlanCreated, pendingStops, runEligibleStops, planFailure, dispatchRoute) are unreachable from the public dispatch entry while planning operations such as savePlan and previewPlan are exported. Importing src/dispatch/index.mjs yields undefined for executeAuthorizedPlan, runEligibleStops and pendingStops. Recommendation: re-export ./executor.mjs from src/dispatch/index.mjs, and ./runtime.mjs if dispatchRoute is part of the caller-facing surface.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, nextRetryDelay applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided retryAfter.
finding: nextRetryDelay tests retryAfter for truthiness instead of applying the Retry timing rules to every finite numeric retryAfter (rule 7). A server-provided retryAfter of 0 is finite numeric but falsy, so the computed backoff replaces the delay the server gave: nextRetryDelay(1, 0) returns 500. A non-numeric retryAfter such as '30' is truthy and is converted by retryAfterDelay even though rule 7 covers only finite numeric values.

requirement: executeAuthorizedPlan rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: executeAuthorizedPlan evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) while building the argument list for unlessForbidden, so dispatch runs for every caller before the authorization result is applied. For an actor with no held scopes and a route depot it does not own, the dispatch callback was invoked once and the call then returned {ok:false,error:'forbidden'}. Recommendation: evaluate canPlanRoute first and return the forbidden result without calling dispatchRoute.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, stopsForDriver returns exactly the stops whose assigned driver is the given driver.
finding: stopsForDriver compares only stop.driver, so it ignores the policy definition of an assigned driver (rule 30: the driver of the stop's reassignment when the stop has one, otherwise the stop's own driver). A stop whose own driver is 'B' but whose reassignment driver is 'A' is not returned for driver 'A'; the probe returns 1 of 2 matching stops. src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:18 applies the rule correctly, so the two operations disagree about the same stops.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, writePlanAtomically renames the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, chooseDeparture applies every Departure timing rule.
finding: chooseDeparture does not apply Departure timing rule 14. A departure chosen inside the departure window (startHour 2, endHour 4) and inside the blackout (startHour 3, endHour 5) is moved to the blackout end hour 05:00 UTC, which lies outside the window, and the moved date is returned instead of being refused: chooseDeparture(2026-01-01T03:30:00Z) returns 2026-01-01T05:00:00.000Z rather than null. Rules 10, 11, 12 and 13 are applied.

evidence.command: node -e "import('./src/dispatch/schedule.mjs').then(s=>{const a=s.chooseDeparture(new Date('2026-01-01T03:30:00Z'));const b=s.nextDispatchTime(new Date('2026-01-01T01:00:00Z'),new Date('2026-01-01T03:30:00Z'));const c=s.nextDispatchTime(new Date('2026-01-01T04:00:00Z'),new Date('2026-01-01T03:00:00Z'));console.log(a.toISOString(),b.toISOString(),c.toISOString())})"

requirement: redactNestedDriverToken removes a nested driver token from telemetry.
emitPlanCreated emits plan.created only after storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated defers the emit into the onCommit option that savePlan passes to store.write, and no governance document in the candidate defines store.write or its onCommit option; docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md specifies only writeTemporary, renameTemporary, discardTemporary and removeTemporary for plans. Whether plan.created is emitted only after storage succeeds therefore depends on an adapter contract that is not available, so the ordering cannot be verified from the staged candidate.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, hasDuplicateRouteKeys reports duplicates exactly when two stops are duplicates.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, parseRetryCount accepts exactly the valid retry counts and otherwise returns an error result.
finding: parseRetryCount coerces with Number() instead of applying retry-count rule 22, so text that is not one or more base-10 digits is accepted: parseRetryCount('') returns ok true with value 0, parseRetryCount(' 2 ') returns ok true, and parseRetryCount('2.0') returns ok true. The returned object also carries no error field for rejected values, so the criterion's error result is not produced.

requirement: remainingVehicleCapacity never returns a negative value.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, pendingStops returns every stop except the delivered stops.
finding: pendingStops excludes only state 'delivered', but policy rule 31 defines a delivered stop as a stop whose state is 'delivered' or 'handedOver', so handedOver stops stay in the pending list. The probe returns the handedOver and open stops for a three-stop input.

requirement: previewPlan returns a dry-run result without invoking storage.
redactAccessLog removes token and secret fields while preserving other fields.
orderedDestinationGroups returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.
finding: orderedDestinationGroups passes the Map returned by groupByDestination into orderManifestGroups, whose declared parameter is an array of group objects. Spreading a Map yields [key, value] entries, so orderedDestinationGroups returns Map entries instead of destination group records, and its comparator reads .destination on those entries as undefined and returns 0 for every pair, so no ordering is applied. orderedDestinationGroups([{destination:'b'},{destination:'a'}]) returns [["B",[{"destination":"B"}]],["A",[{"destination":"A"}]]] in insertion order.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md, routeDistance rejects when no road connects two consecutive points.
savePlan validates a plan before the first persistent write.
computeBackoff doubles from 250 milliseconds and caps the result at 2000 milliseconds.
retryTransient permits retries only for errors explicitly marked transient.
Under docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md, locateStops leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.
finding: locateStops drops a stop only when geocoder.lookup resolves to undefined, but docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md specifies lookup's result only for a known address and never states what lookup does for an address the geocoder does not know. If lookup rejects for an unknown address, the Promise.all in locateStops rejects and the whole call rejects instead of leaving that stop out, so the criterion cannot be settled from the contract as written.

requirement: retainScheduleOffset preserves the supplied offset exactly.
runEligibleStops skips cancelled stops while retaining the other stop order.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, withinVehicleCapacity accepts a total equal to the configured limit.
finding: withinVehicleCapacity compares remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0, so a total exactly equal to the configured limit leaves zero remaining capacity and is rejected. withinVehicleCapacity(10000, 10) returns false, and canAssignAllPackages([{weight:6000},{weight:4000}], 10) returns false, although the package total in grams equals the 10 kilogram limit from policy rules 28 and 29. The comparison must accept equality.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, canPlanRoute treats an actor holding routes:admin as owning every depot.
finding: canPlanRoute applies the admin override with actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin'), but policy rule 4 defines an actor's held scopes as its own scopes plus the scope of every active claim. An actor that holds routes:admin only through an active claim is refused for a depot it does not equal: canPlanRoute({depotId:'D1',scopes:[],claims:[{scope:'routes:admin',startsAt:0,expiresAt:10}]},{depotId:'D2'},5) returns false. The override should test the held scopes that effectiveScopes already computes.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, canPlanRoute refuses every suspended actor.
selectActiveClaims excludes claims before their start and at or after expiry.
checksumPlan hashes the bytes returned by the plan serializer.
Connect dispatch manifest publication through the public dispatch entry.
safeAnnouncement omits a top-level credential from the announcement payload.
encodeUtf8 encodes publication bytes as UTF-8.
manifestEntryIsValid rejects blank package IDs.
Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, publishWithAnnouncement removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, redactManifestEvent removes every credential nested below an auth field.
Given a positive integer maximum, chunkManifest limits every non-empty chunk to that configured maximum.
Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, publishWithAnnouncement waits for the exact manifest to be durably stored before sending its announcement.
serializeManifestRecords emits NDJSON with one LF after every record, including the last.
orderManifestGroups orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, manifestRecipients lists the contact phone of every manifest entry that has a phone.
publicationResult returns structured success and failure variants.
normalizedPlanKey trims and uppercases the route-key storage segment.
buildManifest copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.
finding: buildManifest spreads each record but reuses the record's driver object: labelDriver applies Object.assign(driver, {label: ...}) to that shared object, so the label write mutates the supplied record and the manifest entry is the very same object rather than a copy. In the probe, manifest.entries[0].driver === rec.driver is true and a later change to rec.driver.label is visible through the built manifest.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, publishWithRetry stops after the allowed number of publication attempts.
publishManifest stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.
finding: publishManifest builds checks with an async arrow, so every element is a Promise, and Promise objects are always truthy, which makes checks.every(Boolean) always true and the validity gate unreachable. publishManifest stored a manifest containing the blank packageId '  ' and performed one store.put call while returning {ok:true}. Recommendation: validate entries synchronously with manifestEntryIsValid before calling stageManifest.

requirement: successTelemetry records the success event, manifest ID, and timestamp.
groupByDestination groups records using normalized destination keys.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, departureMinute is a stop's arrivalMinute plus its service time.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, publishWithRetry retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.
preserveManifestDriver trims driver labels without changing letter case.
coalescePackages removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.
Stop ordering uses descending priority followed by ascending sequence.
Publication audit records include action, actor, and timestamp.
Window membership includes both the declared start and end hour.
Schedule offsets pass through without coercion.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.
finding: routeDuration sums stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes for every stop, but policy rule 32 defines a stop's service time as its serviceMinutes plus 5 minutes of parking, so every stop is understated by 5 minutes: routeDuration([{travelMinutes:10,serviceMinutes:5}]) returns 15 instead of 20. src/dispatch/schedule.mjs:28 applies the +5 for a single stop, so the two operations disagree about the same stop.

requirement: Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.
Empty manifests use an empty entries array and a generated marker.
Publication failure telemetry includes the manifest ID, error, and timestamp.
Driver labels are trimmed without changing their letter case.
savePlan completes validation before its first write.
Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.
Package IDs are trimmed, deduplicated, and sorted lexically.
Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.
Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.
Under docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md, publishManifest returns, in a success result, the manifest object that store.put durably stored.
Eligible-stop execution excludes cancelled stops.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.
finding: canAssignAllPackages delegates to withinVehicleCapacity, which compares remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0, so a package total exactly equal to the vehicle limit leaves zero remaining capacity and is rejected: canAssignAllPackages([{weight:6000},{weight:4000}], 10) returns false and withinVehicleCapacity(10000, 10) returns false, although the gram total equals the 10 kilogram limit from policy rules 28 and 29.

requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.
finding: src/dispatch/index.mjs re-exports eleven dispatch modules but omits src/dispatch/executor.mjs and src/dispatch/runtime.mjs, so the execution operations that callers use (executeAuthorizedPlan, executeDryRun, emitPlanCreated, pendingStops, planFailure, runEligibleStops, dispatchRoute) are not exported from the public dispatch entry; importing src/dispatch/index.mjs yields undefined for executeAuthorizedPlan, runEligibleStops and pendingStops.

requirement: Publication success telemetry includes the manifest ID and timestamp.
Plan previews return without touching persistent storage.
Appending a stable stop returns a new list.
Dispatch backoff is capped at 2000 milliseconds.
Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.
Transient retry classification requires an explicit true marker.
Depot ownership requires equal actor and route depot identifiers.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.
finding: partitionUrgentStops filters urgent with priorityOf(stop) > 5 but filters remaining with !(stop.priority > 5), bypassing the policy rule 15 default for a stop without a finite numeric priority. Such a stop matches neither filter and lands in no partition: partitionUrgentStops([{id:1,priority:'9'}]) returns urgent [] and remaining [], so 0 of 1 input stops is placed.

requirement: Destination keys are normalized with NFKC, trimmed, and uppercased.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.
finding: nextDispatchTime tests candidate.getHours(), the host time zone hour, instead of the UTC hour required by rule 10, so the blackout adjustment is applied to the wrong hour. With the configured blackout at 03:00-05:00 UTC on this UTC+9 host, nextDispatchTime(2026-01-01T01:00:00Z, 2026-01-01T03:30:00Z) returns 2026-01-01T03:30:00.000Z and nextDispatchTime(2026-01-01T04:00:00Z, 2026-01-01T03:00:00Z) returns 2026-01-01T04:00:00.000Z, so neither candidate inside the blackout is moved to the blackout end hour as rule 13 requires.

Manifest NDJSON ends every record, including the final record, with LF.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.

Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.
finding: authorizeRouteBatch returns firstRejected <= 0, so it rejects only when the very first route fails depot ownership and accepts a batch whose failure appears at any later index. authorizeRouteBatch({depotId:'D1'},[{depotId:'D2'},{depotId:'D1'}]) returns true although the first route fails, and a batch whose only failure is at index 1 or beyond is also accepted. The check should be firstRejected === -1.

requirement: Successful publication results and failed publication results use distinct structured variants.
Blank package IDs make a manifest entry invalid.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, a driver's workload counts exactly the stops whose assigned driver is that driver.
Under docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.
